content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text weighs the challenger's seed/loins chain against the defender's chain over one link (D6 vs C1), which is exactly the chain-against-chain collision this rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "The phrase 'never verse by verse' joined with 'no one of them states the contrary in its own words': on one reading a judge may still fault a footed chain because no verse names its conclusion in so many words, on the other a judge who finds both chains footed must weigh footing alone and may not discount either chain for not stating its point in its own words.", "why": "The judge found both chains footed yet rested its UNDERDETERMINED verdict on the lack of word-for-word statement ('does not name Joseph as the begetter', 'rests on the woman-route inference'), applying the retired stating-verse test against both sides instead of weighing footing alone."}
